keystores.note: Separate keys for the liquidity and team roles. At deployment neither held ETH, and the liquidity address needed gas before it could seed the pool.

supply.communityHolder: The community and ecosystem share is held by AdminTimelock, so every release is a two-of-three proposal with the same 172800-second delay as any other change.
supply.teamHolder: The team share is held by the Vesting contract. One grant, four-year term, one-year cliff, and the deploy key finished the run holding no BRSR at all.

parameters.staking.unbondingPeriod: 604800 seconds, the contract's own seven-day floor.
parameters.staking.minBondWei: 25000000000000000000000, which is 25,000 BRSR per resolver. Set at construction because the dispute layer reads it from the first block, and a pool deployed at zero would ship a dispute layer no resolver could join until a forty-eight hour proposal landed. Governance can raise it globally or per resolver and OracleRegistry reads it live on every vote.
parameters.buyback.maxPriceMicroUsdPerBrsr: 0, deployed from an unset variable on purpose. It is the most a buyback will pay for one whole BRSR, and the pool was not initialised at deployment, so there was no price to read. Zero refuses every trade: buyback() reverts with PriceCeilingUnset and available() reports nothing.
parameters.why these figures: Sized to the float Release 1 had at deployment, below the round numbers in contracts/script/TOKEN-README.md. The buyback can only spend what has been transferred to it, and a per-call target above the balance would never be the binding constraint. All six move on a Buyback.setParams proposal; only the pool identity is frozen.

verifiedOnChain.bytecode: The deployed runtime of BRSR, Vesting, Staking and Buyback matches the contracts/out build byte for byte once the immutable words each constructor writes are masked out, which read as zero in the artifact. Checked at block 69566482 by reading eth_getCode and masking the immutableReferences spans in both copies. PoolManager is Uniswap's and was not compared. Source comments naming the previous chain were corrected after this check. Solidity hashes the source into a metadata word at the end of the runtime, so the current build no longer reproduces those trailing bytes. That match was made against the source as it stood at deployment; later changes to these contracts ship as a new deployment. Every byte of executable code is unchanged, verified by rebuilding with the metadata suffix stripped and comparing: BRSR 7,533 bytes, Buyback 9,530, Staking 9,786, Vesting 5,238, AgentRegistry 11,374, all identical.

governance.model: Two of three signers with a forty-eight hour delay and a fourteen-day grace period after it. Proposing counts as the proposer's approval, so a change needs one more signer and not two, and any single signer can cancel a pending one. The guardian is the one exception to the delay: it can pause an administered contract in the same block and can do nothing else.

adminOf.BRSR: No admin role. Fixed supply, no minter, no owner, no upgrade path.

usdgCompliance.finding: USDG is a diamond proxy. It routes paused() and isFrozen(address) and reverts FacetNotFound on anything it does not route, isBlacklisted and version() included. Both reads are ordinary storage behind a delegatecall with no precompile in the path, so they are read straight, with no gas stipend and no three-valued answer.

pending: At block 69575881 Staking.creditManager was unset, and Staking.slash and Staking.distribute refused every caller. The credit pool that charges the spread arrived with the second contract set, and naming it is a v1 timelock proposal recorded in rhc-mainnet-v2.json.

At block 69575881 the buyback's price ceiling was zero and every call reverted with PriceCeilingUnset. Governance sets a real one through Buyback.setParams now that the pool has a price, and that proposal has to land before the buyback is funded.
At block 69575881 the staking pool held no shares, so a buyback would have reverted with NoStakeToDistributeTo before it traded, even with a ceiling and a seeded pool.
audit: No external review has been performed on any of these contracts.
